title: Canonical determinant norm equals affine chart norm
statement: Let A and B be commutative rings and φ : A → B a unital map whose affine spectrum morphism [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is finite locally free of constant degree r [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. For b ∈ B, let Nφ(b) be the canonical determinant norm selected by the unique local determinant characterization in [lem-a1-finite-locally-free-norm-characteristic-polynomial]. Then every x ∈ Spec A has an affine open V containing x on which Γ(Spec B, φ⁻¹V) is finite free over Γ(Spec A,V), and the restriction of Nφ(b) equals the finite free algebra norm of the restriction of b. Equivalently this value is computed by the determinant of multiplication in any finite basis of that section algebra. Zero rings, rank zero, zero section rings and empty inverse images are allowed.

source.place: Tags 02DU(1), 02DV(1),(3), and Tag 03BJ, second paragraph: local determinant norm and affine-open norm comparison.

proof.text: Apply the principal basis cover theorem [lem-a1-finite-locally-free-principal-basis-cover] to obtain a unit-ideal family and localized rank-r bases, plus quasi-coherence of the structure-sheaf pushforward. First identify the two scalar module structures on each localization: on fractions (a/s) and (b/t), both act by (ab)/(st), so Module.ext identifies them, including zero localizations. Transport each basis through the canonical localization-tensor equivalence. The multiplication matrices then agree definitionally. The uniqueness clause of the principal-free determinant norm theorem [lem-a1-principal-free-algebra-determinant-norm] identifies the canonical norm [lem-a1-finite-locally-free-norm-characteristic-polynomial] with principalFreeNorm. At each point use the finite-locally-free norm-chart theorem [lem-pd-finite-locally-free-norm-charts] to obtain a free affine chart, discarding its auxiliary norm section. Take an arbitrary finite basis (reindexed by Fin, without assuming the section ring is nonzero). Apply the affine-open clause of the principal-free norm theorem and Algebra.norm_eq_matrix_det; both are the determinant of multiplication by the restricted element. This gives the asserted formula. Empty spectra have no points to check; zero section algebras and rank-zero bases obey the same determinant formula.
